recipes.name: Potatoes and Peppers
ingredients_raw: 2 large red bell peppers, sliced into rings
1 large sweet onion, peeled and chopped

steps.text: Heat oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add potatoes and fry for 5 minutes. Add peppers and onions, then season with salt and pepper. Cook until potatoes look very soft, turning frequently, at least 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Potatoes and Peppers
raw_recipe.description: Instead of roasting potatoes and peppers, pull out your frying pan and sauté them with onions for an equally tasty treat in just 20 minutes.

review.reviewBody: What, no garlic, no herbs, no spices, you say? Yep, none of the above, and delicious all on its own, with just a little salt and pepper (and a mix of olive oil and bacon grease, not measured, just what I needed). Tender skinned tiny new potatoes made this particulary pretty and tasty.

Great recipe! Reminded me of restaurant potatoes! I used about half the oil since my pan was nonstick and it wasn't greasy at all. I don't like my potatoes quite so blackened so I cooked the potatoes in the microwave for about 6-7 minutes while I fried the onions and peppers.

This was a really great dish! I added some turkey kielbasa to the mix to make it more of a main dish and the added flavor was wonderful. 

I cut down on the oil & did a mixture of rosemary, garlic, and hot pepper infused oils which I sauted the potatoes, onions & some fresh thyme in for about 10 mins. I then added a 1/2 c. of chicken stock & put the lid on to allow them to soften up. In a grill pan I roasted the sliced peppers to give them a nice grilled flavor then added them to the potatoes & onions. I seasoned the dish with adobo, garlic salt, and white pepper to taste. On the grill pan I sauted turkey kielbasa and added it to the veggie mix once it was done. I let all of the ingredients cook for about 5-10 mins more to combine the flavors and it came out awesome! We will be having this again for sure.

One of my favorite mixtures, everyone seems to like it. Also put in green pepper in addition to red for color and roast in oven at 400 for about 35-40 min or till potatoes done and turning the mixture once or twice. We like garlic so usually also add some fresh or powdered. This is also good with half white and half sweet potato.

There is a chain of rotisserie chicken stores in Mexico and they cook whole, small potatoes directly under the roasting chickens so the juices drip onto the potatoes while they are cooking. I added an infrared burner to my old BBQ so I could use my rotisserie without burning up the chicken and adding potatoes was only natural. I start out by placing my cast iron skillet directly under the chicken to collect all of the juices. About 30 minutes before the chicken is done I add the potatoes, onions, and bell peppers and cook as directed in this recipe. The last time I had to add a little water because the ingredients were beginning to stick and it worked like magic. This recipe is perfect with rotisserie chicken.

We’ve had this dish as a family heritage dish for at least 5 generations. There is a big difference though. To get the great texture and goodness, we slice the potatoes quite
 thin. And use a large cast iron skillet. We call them Grandpa Potatoes. The bacon grease at the start and a large dollop of butter or margarine 5 minutes before fully browned plus ground black pepper and Lawry’s seasoning salt makes this a crowd pleaser.
This is a good recipe. Instread of frying I put the whole thing in the oven. Next time I will remove the lid so it will brown up.

The recipe shown is very simple to make and quick, so it is good.
I do a few things differently. I use frozen Oreida Potatoes that won't get mushy if you add them just before the onions and peppers are cooked so that they will be tender but firm. This works great and taste very good.
I use regular cooking oil to caramelized the onions with the peppers cooking them about 15 mins on a lower heat and not stirring them until translucent. 
Since I use this recipe to make Italian hotdogs, I add a tsp. of Intalian seasoning, salt and pepper to taste.
You don't have to use oilive oil to pan cook the vegetables, but you can finish the dish off with a little of the oil poured over it.

This was amazing! I pre cooked potatoes cooked up the bacon onion and peppers added garlic … then did the potatoes until they were brown … tossed through the pepper mix and sprinkled with dill … new staple for sure !!
My MOM use to scramble a couple of eggs and add it, was my dad's favorite dish

Love this as a side dish with steak or beef tips. Substituting garlic infused oil for plain olive oil really boosts the flavor. I also prefer to substitute some of the sweet onion with shallots for a little complexity.
I love how the little potatoes I used dotted the pan; in between chunks of peppers and onions. And the potatoes were red, the peppers green, and the onions, white. And, the were as tasty as it looked
I forgot the potatoes but added Broccoli, Zucchini & Cabbage! Was wonderful , simple & Healthy!
I use roasted garlic in herd instead of salt and pepper.
I have been making this dish for years.

Don’t know if it was my cast iron pan? The thickness of the potatoes? These were good but just that. They definitely looked pretty and appealing but flavor was only okay. Might try again but slightly pre-cook before starting the frying. Thanks!
I have made these for years I've added keilbassa, mild yellow peppers anything you like we love them any time other day...
Very tasty, and as a bonus it was easy to make. Will make this again and again as a breakfast side dish.
Have made many times now. Great taste quick and easy.
